headline: Japan's Press Dismantled Tunisia in Four Acts
story: Japan struck inside four minutes and never looked back, setting a tempo Tunisia couldn't sustain. The defining metric was intensity: Japan's 3.6 high-press phases overwhelmed Tunisia's fragile 1.9, creating a pace the North Africans simply couldn't absorb. By half-time, Japan led 2-0 with 55% possession against Tunisia's 36%; the visitors had mustered just two shots. The match's shape was irreversibly settled before the break.

Japan's dominance crystallised in the numbers. Their ball recovery time of 13.7 seconds against Tunisia's 22.1 gave them an eight-second edge that proved fatal in a game decided by tempo. Ayase Ueda (9.3 rating) and Ko Itakura (8.5) controlled midfield, with Daichi Kamada (7.8) providing rhythm. Tunisia mustered 0.02 expected goals across 90 minutes; Japan finished four, clinical conversions of their 1.36 xG advantage.

keyMoment.text: Japan's early goal set an unrecoverable precedent—Tunisia chased shadows thereafter.

home.verdict: Overmatched at every layer; Group F will demand sharper execution.
points: High-press disparity (1.9 vs 3.6 phases) meant no sustained offensive pressure; need chances created per match.
Ball recovery at 22.1 seconds left them perpetually chasing; eight-second gap to Japan proved fatal.
Zero on-target shots, 0.02 xG: didn't create or threaten—must add a playmaker who unpicks defences.

away.verdict: Ruthless execution and pressing intelligence justified pre-tournament billing.
points: Press intensity at 3.6 phases dismantled Tunisia's rhythm; replicate this template against stronger sides.
Ball recovery in 13.7 seconds enabled control; maintain this eight-second edge via transition drills.
Survived early sloppiness (two big chances missed, 0.35 combined xG) but clinical finishing sealed it—don't expect that mercy twice.

statLine: Japan's eight-second ball recovery advantage (13.7 to 22.1 seconds) translated into four goals and complete dismantling of Tunisia's Group F opener.
